title: You’re 18. What’s next?
lesson: Your starting circumstances shape the choices available to you.

choices.title: Uni
choices.description: Study, work part-time, and take on tuition debt

title: Give yourself a cushion?
body: Add $200 from your pay to an emergency fund?
lesson: An emergency fund keeps a small surprise from becoming a bigger money problem.

choices.title: Yes — save $200
choices.description: Move $200 from cash to your emergency fund

title: Unexpected expense!
body: You snuck into a frat party and got frat flu! Medical bills are $200.
lesson: Emergency savings give you options when life gets expensive.

choices.title: Take money from my emergency fund
choices.description: Use your cushion to cover the $200 bill

choices.title: Call Mom to ask for money :(
choices.description: Ask for a $200 family gift to cover the bill

title: Happy birthday!
body: You got $1,000. What would you like to do with it?
lesson: An account is a container; choosing an investment is a separate decision.

choices.title: Open an account
choices.description: Choose TFSA, RRSP, or FHSA · keep the gift ready to invest

choices.title: Buy BizTech
choices.description: Invest the $1,000 gift in one company

choices.title: Put it in a savings account
choices.description: Save $1,000 separately from your emergency fund

title: You got a raise!
body: A 10% raise on $30,000/year gives you an extra $250 each month. How would you like to invest?
lesson: A raise can fund your future before it becomes a new spending habit.

title: Your money made a move
body: What would you like to do with this money?
lesson: Sometimes taking risk helps. Not always. A good month is not a promise about the next one.

choices.title: Buy a penthouse in Miami
choices.description: Check your shortfall against a $1,000,000 penthouse

choices.title: Continue investing in high risk
choices.description: Move your portfolio to QQQ for this demo

choices.title: Invest in low risk
choices.description: Move your portfolio to VAB · lower risk still has risk
